questions.question_text: Which one among the following is an early sign of opioid withdrawal?
questions.explanation:
Early signs and symptoms of opioid withdrawal starts within 6-12 hours for short-acting drugs, and 24- 36 hours for longer-acting drugs.
Symptoms include muscle aches, anxiety and agitation, sleep issues, running nose and yawning. Nausea and vomiting, diarrhoea, goose
bumps, stomach cramps, depression or dysphoria and intense drug cravings start later (late onset symptoms)

To explore the e�ects of clinical supervision on the study strategies used by undergraduate medical students during their clinical rotations,
a phenomenological study was carried out from November 2007 to December 2008. Semi-structured focus groups interviews for students in
clinical years (3 and 4 of the 4 year programme) and individual interviews for teachers and students were conducted to explore students'
and clinical teachers' perceptions and interpretations of factors in�uencing students' study strategies. All interviews were open-ended and
were conducted by the principal investigator and a research assistant. Both students and teachers were allowed to talk freely and express
their opinion on the e�ects of clinical supervision, patient encounters and assessment characteristics on students' adopted study strategies.
For triangulation of the data, the authors conducted a second set of interviews with all of the 13 clinical teachers and 12 of the students who
had participated in the focus groups. They were asked about their opinions on the results of the �rst round of students' focus group
interviews. The obtained themes were used to analyse the whole dataset and rearrange the data according to the themes and sub-themes.
All interviews were transcribed verbatim and themes and sub-themes relevant to the research questions were assigned and representing
quotes were selected. This process was repeated for each interview in order to capture the full breadth and diversity of the students' and
teachers' views and experiences. A Computer Software Atlas-ti (Version 5.2) was used to apply the themes to the whole dataset and to
rearrange the data according to themes and sub- themes. Analysis of data from interviews with twenty-eight students and thirteen clinical
supervisors yielded three major themes relating to factors a�ecting students' study strategies: "clinical supervisors and supervision", "stress
and anxiety" and "assessment". The three themes we identi�ed played a role in students' adoption of di�erent study strategies in the
"community of clinical practice". It appeared that teachers played a key role, particularly as assessors, clinical supervisors and as a source of
stress to students. ( What type of study is this?
questions.explanation:
Phenomenological studies are qualitative in nature. Other pointers in the precis include triangulation, focus groups, open-ended questions
and semi-structured interviews.

questions.question_text: Which of the following symptom is most likely in a patient with severe and acute lithium toxicity?
questions.explanation:
Patients with acute lithium elevation predominantly su�er from nausea, vomiting, cramping, and sometimes diarrhea. Progression to severe
toxicity can involve neuromuscular signs such as tremulousness (coarse tremors), dystonia, hyperre�exia, and ataxia. Toxic e�ects occur at
levels of >1.5 mmol/L. Above 2 m mol/L, increased disorientation and seizures usually occur, which can progress to coma and ultimately
death.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most common ECG �nding in a patient with acute lithium toxicity?
questions.explanation:
Lithium toxicity induces various ECG changes – the most common of these is nonspeci�c T-wave �attening followed by dysfunction of sinus
node and prolonged QTc.

questions.question_text: The most likely reason to transfer an anorexic patient in a psychiatric ward to a medical unit is
questions.explanation:
Please be aware of the MARSIPAN report produced by the RCPsych Working Group (which provides comprehensive guidelines on managing very sick patients with anorexia nervosa. A signi�cant increase in QT and QTc, can
result from weight loss in patients with anorexia nervosa (Vázquez et al., 2003). Due to the elevated risk of sudden cardiac death, patients
with QTc prolongation should be medically managed.

questions.question_text: The most likely electrolyte abnormality of refeeding a grossly anorexic patient in a medical ward is
questions.explanation:
Excerpt from MARSIPAN report "In an acute medical service (Gaudiani et al, 2012) 45% of patients developed hypophosphataemia and in
French intensive care units (Vignaud et al, 2010) 11% of patients developed re-feeding syndrome. It appears, therefore, that the highest rate
of re-feeding syndrome is reported from the units in which patients are most unwell, namely adult medical and intensive care setting".
As noted in multiple sources, including MARSIPAN (Management of Really Sick Patients with Anorexia Nervosa), the potentially fatal
refeeding syndrome is caused by the switch from fasting gluconeogenesis to carbohydrate-induced insulin release, inducing considerable
intracellular uptake of potassium, phosphate, and magnesium from the bloodstream. This can cause profound biochemical derangements
including hypokalaemia, hypophosphataemia, hypomagnesaemia, and occasionally hypocalcaemia.
Ref: Morris J, Anderson S. An update on eating disorders. BJPsych Advances. 2020:1-11.
Taylor DM, Gaughran F, Pillinger T. The Maudsley Practice Guidelines for Physical Health Conditions in Psychiatry. 2021.

options.text: Reduce venlafaxine and mirtazapine and add lithium

questions.explanation:
According to BAP guidelines, "consider adding quetiapine (A), aripiprazole (A) or lithium (A) as �rst-line treatments, and risperidone (A),
olanzapine (B), tri-iodothyronine (B) or mirtazapine (B) as second-line treatments, being aware that the evidence derives mainly from studies
in which lithium and tri-iodothyronine were added to TCAs and the other drugs added to SSRI/SNRIs". Assuming that lithiumaugmentation of
a SSRI/SNRI has not been triedyet, we can chose to add lithium to venlafaxine.

questions.question_text: What is the chance of 40-year-old mother giving birth to a child with Down syndrome?
questions.explanation:
With increasing age, the risk of giving birth to a child with Down syndrome greatly increases (2 to 3 times increase in risk every 5 years). By
age 35, the absolute risk for a pregnant mother 1 in 350. By age 40, it bounces to 1 in 100, and by age 45, it peaks to 1 in 30. Ref:

questions.question_text: A girl who attends a mainstream school with apparently normal IQ has visuospatial di�culties. The most likely diagnosis is
questions.explanation:
Turner syndrome is relatively common (1/2,500 women) in a phenotypic female. It is associated with a cognitive pro�le of normal intellectual
and verbal function but impairments in visual–spatial, executive, and social cognitive domains.

questions.question_text:
A patient who had a severe episode of herpes encephalitis 3 months ago recovered fully but now su�ers from new-onset carbohydrate
craving. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.explanation:
Hyperorality, hypersexuality, and abnormal eating behaviour characterized by carbohydrate craving after herpes encephalitis is suggestive
of Kluver-Bucy syndrome resulting from medial temporal lobe damage.

questions.question_text: What is most likely drug associated with gum bleeding?
questions.explanation:
Non-GI bleeds such as gum bleeds and subconjunctival bleeds are rare with SSRIs. Carbamazepine can cause gingival bleeds due to their
propensity to reduce platelet levels. Other antiepileptic drugs that can cause gingival bleed include levatiracetam and phenytoin.

questions.question_text: Which of the following medications can cause fatal intestinal obstruction?
questions.explanation:
Rapidly fatal intestinal obstruction has been reported with clozapine, sometimes even without prior warning signs. Some case reports also
implicate risperidone and olanzapine in intestinal obstructions.

questions.question_text: Ebstein's anomaly is sometimes associated with drugs other than lithium. Choose one such drug:
questions.explanation:
Genetic, reproductive, and environmental risk factors can contribute to Ebstein's anomaly. It is more common in twins, in those with a family
history of congenital heart disease, and in those with maternal exposure to lithium or benzodiazepines. But most cases are sporadic. Ref:

questions.question_text: A major aim of interpersonal therapy for depression is
questions.explanation:
Resolving an interpersonal struggle in a role dispute is one of the primary aims of IPT. Whether life events follow or precede mood changes,
the patient's task in therapy is to resolve the disturbing life event(s), building social skills and helping to organize his or her life. Excerpt from:

questions.question_text: The three R's of Cognitive Analytical Therapy are:
questions.explanation: The three R's of Cognitive Analytical Therapy are Reformulation, Recognition and Revision.

questions.question_text: The type of family therapy that depends on transactions is:
questions.explanation:
A family establishes a set of rules for its daily functioning through its transactions. According to structural family therapy, these rules form a
family unit's structure.
